name: Head-to-Head Comparison Ad
description: A vertical 9:16 'pick a side' head-to-head product-comparison short (~60-70s) built as ONE HyperFrames composition: sequential <video> / still clips on a single track 0 carry the two paths (the SAFE brand vs the BAD brand), while a stack of ALWAYS-PRESENT overlay divs — a film-leader countdown, a depleting LIMITS/credit gauge, kinetic captions, an end-card — are gated open/closed by one paused GSAP timeline. The comparison reads on color and a draining meter, not narration: one side is a calm accent with 'no meter, no countdown'; the other side is the opposite accent where a battery-style gauge drains 100%->0% on the viewer's behalf and flips danger-red at zero. Load-bearing mechanics: gauge = scaleX fill + onUpdate percent counter on a proxy tween (slow drain, 1s crash on the trigger beat); countdown = SVG ring strokeDashoffset sweep per second; ALL labels/wordmarks are a VT323-style overlay in HyperFrames, never baked into generated frames (the image model smudges text); hold ONE aesthetic end-to-end (the source's single biggest miss was the SAFE montage breaking register). Every background is a still with a slow Ken-Burns push-in; scene changes are 0.5s opacity crossfades, never hard cuts. Locations + motion are AI-generated (gemini-3-pro-image multi-ref for identity lock, seedance-2.0 for plunges, wan-2.7 for cheap push-ins); VHS / grade is a post-process ffmpeg pass.
referenceNotes: If remixing a specific source clip, ref-pull it for the cut blueprint + reusable keyframes. The two brands' identities lock via multi-ref (master + character + source-frame) on every gemini gen.
